title: validate
description: Format validation behavior of Triauth.validate({identifier?, deviceName?}). validate is synchronous and pure - it touches no DNS, clock, or randomness - so dnsEntries/currentTime are present only for schema parity and are ignored. These cases alone exercise every reachable branch of validate() (validation.js. NOTE: the null/non-object/array early-return inside hasOnlyKnownProperties is unreachable from validate (the code 101 guard rejects those inputs first), and the 'whitelisted-key-with-undefined-value' rejection inside it is not expressible in JSON (JSON has no undefined); both are therefore intentionally uncovered by this JSON suite.

ARG GUARD 101: empty object -> Object.keys(objects).length === 0 operand

CONFIG GUARD 103: a valid config override is accepted and object validation proceeds (valid identifier -> valid:true)
CONFIG GUARD 103: the objects guard takes precedence - a bad objects key returns 102 even when config is also misspelled

tests.name: IDENTIFIER valid: exactly 120 bytes (identifierBytesize) passes - the byteSize check is strict-greater, pinning the boundary against off-by-one ports
IDENTIFIER 212: one byte over identifierBytesize (121 > 120) is rejected - the boundary-negative twin of the 120-byte positive
IDENTIFIER valid: name-part at exactly 63 characters (the grammar cap: alnum *62) passes
IDENTIFIER 215: name-part of 64 characters exceeds the 63-character grammar cap (alnum *62) while staying under the identifierBytesize total
IDENTIFIER 215: a plus sign in the username (john+work) is rejected - '+' is not a username character
IDENTIFIER 210: embedded NUL (U+0000) is rejected by the same whitespace-and-NUL check, not the grammar
IDENTIFIER 216: IPv4-literal domain (john@1.2.3.4) - a numeric final label is never a domain part
IDENTIFIER 216: all-digits final label (john@example.99) - real TLDs are never numeric
IDENTIFIER 216: 0x-hex final label (john@example.0xff) - exotic IPv4 spellings fall to the same numeric-final-label rule
IDENTIFIER valid: domain label at exactly 63 characters (the DNS label cap) passes
IDENTIFIER 216: domain label of 64 characters exceeds the 63-character DNS label cap while staying under the identifierBytesize total
IDENTIFIER 216: single-character final label (john@a.b) - a final label is at least two characters
DEVICENAME valid: exactly 20 bytes (the cap) passes - strict-greater check, boundary companion of the 262 case
